answer: Each identity claims one cell on a trellis lattice frozen into a glacier snapshot. The claimant locks 70, pays 20, finishes that cell's work, and hands it to a raven courier with a key-signed receipt. Any checker can recompute snapshot, claim, match, and signature. A rented parcel fails: receipt key mismatches the claimant, its cell already claimed, so the claim is rejected and the bond burns. The kth fake pays 90, its bond, fee, and work, as cells and receipts are single-use; 1,000 fakes lock 70,000 plus 20,000 in fees. An honest identity pays 90 once and recovers 70 after a clean epoch.
